title: Difference Between Maximum and Minimum Price Sum
summary: Given an undirected tree with n nodes indexed from 0 to n-1 , and an integer array price where price[i] is the price of the i -th node, you need to determine the maximum possible cost.
statement: Given an undirected tree with n nodes indexed from 0 to n-1 , and an integer array price where price[i] is the price of the i -th node, you need to determine the maximum possible cost. The cost is defined as the difference between the maximum and minimum price sums of all paths starting from any chosen root node. The tree can be rooted at any node, and the price sum of a path is the sum of the prices of all nodes on that path. Return the largest possible cost among all possible root choices.
constraints: The edges form a connected undirected tree and every node price is positive.
For a chosen root, consider sums of all paths starting at that root, including the root-only path.
Return the largest possible difference between maximum and minimum path sums over every root choice.
reference_solution:
def maximum_root_path_difference(n,edges,price):
    graph=[[] for _ in range(n)]
    for left,right in edges:graph[left].append(right);graph[right].append(left)
    answer=0
    def visit(node,parent):
        nonlocal answer
        included=price[node];excluded=0
        for neighbor in graph[node]:
            if neighbor==parent:continue
            child_included,child_excluded=visit(neighbor,node)
            answer=max(answer,included+child_excluded,excluded+child_included)
            included=max(included,price[node]+child_included)
            excluded=max(excluded,price[node]+child_excluded)
        return included,excluded
    visit(0,-1)
    return answer

hints: Because prices are positive, the minimum path from a root is its root-only path.
At each node track the best downward path including its endpoint and the best variant excluding one endpoint price.
Combine one child path with the best accumulated path from previously processed branches before updating either state.
Every candidate optimal path has a unique highest joining node; the paired included/excluded states count its prices exactly once.
